brief.subject: FTC targets hidden fees and data-driven personalized pricing
brief.headline: FTC Sues Toast Over Hidden Fees, Probes Personalized Pricing at Nine Firms
brief.dek: Regulators sued Toast over hidden fees and cancellation tactics and ordered airlines, ride-hailing and delivery firms to explain data-based pricing.
brief.lede: Federal and state regulators are cracking down on hidden fees and hard-to-cancel subscriptions. The FTC is also asking whether your personal data shapes the prices you're charged.

sections.heading: FTC and States Sue Toast
bullets: The FTC, California local officials and attorneys general from seven states sued Toast Inc., a restaurant software and fintech company.
The complaint alleges hidden and unauthorized fees, a pattern worth watching on any bill you receive.
Regulators also accuse Toast of deceptive subscription and cancellation practices, a growing enforcement focus.
The agencies say Toast misled customers about costs and its promised "24/7/365" customer support.

sections.heading: Is Your Data Setting Your Price?
bullets: The FTC ordered nine major airlines, ride-sharing companies and food-delivery firms to hand over detailed information.
Regulators want to learn how these companies use personal data to set prices, which could mean different shoppers pay different amounts.
The inquiry also covers how personal data shapes compensation, such as what drivers and couriers are paid.
This is a study, not an enforcement action, so no company has been accused of wrongdoing yet.
